histology__BASIC TISSUES__Connective Tis.question: Reticular fibres form the framework of organs such as the liver and lymph node. What are they, and how are they best demonstrated?
histology__BASIC TISSUES__Connective Tis.explanation: Reticular fibres are type III collagen; they are invisible on H&E and are shown black by silver (reticulin) staining, outlining organ stroma.

histology__BASIC TISSUES__Connective Tis.question: Which fibre type provides stretch and recoil and requires a special stain (e.g. Verhoeff) to visualise?
histology__BASIC TISSUES__Connective Tis.explanation: Elastic fibres (elastin + fibrillin) give tissues stretch and recoil (large arteries, some ligaments) and need an elastic stain to be seen on section.

histology__BASIC TISSUES__Connective Tis.question: A tendon is composed of which connective tissue?
histology__BASIC TISSUES__Connective Tis.explanation: Tendons (and ligaments/aponeuroses) are dense regular connective tissue — parallel collagen bundles giving tensile strength in one direction.

histology__BASIC TISSUES__Connective Tis.question: The dermis and organ capsules, which must resist tension from many directions, are made of:
histology__BASIC TISSUES__Connective Tis.explanation: Dense irregular connective tissue has collagen bundles running in random directions, resisting multidirectional tension — as in the dermis, capsules, submucosa and periosteum.

histology__BASIC TISSUES__Connective Tis.question: Which connective tissue is the general-purpose 'packing material' found in the lamina propria beneath epithelia?
histology__BASIC TISSUES__Connective Tis.explanation: Loose (areolar) CT — with all fibre types, many cells and abundant ground substance — is the general support/packing tissue, e.g. the lamina propria.

histology__BASIC TISSUES__Connective Tis.question: Brown adipose tissue differs from white adipose in that it is:
options: Multilocular with many mitochondria and generates heat via UCP1
A type of dense regular tissue
histology__BASIC TISSUES__Connective Tis.explanation: Brown fat is multilocular (many small droplets, central nucleus) and mitochondria-rich; it produces heat by UCP1-mediated thermogenesis and is prominent in neonates. White fat is unilocular (signet-ring) for storage.

histology__BASIC TISSUES__Connective Tis.question: A hyperflexible patient with stretchy, fragile skin and easy bruising most likely has a defect in:
histology__BASIC TISSUES__Connective Tis.explanation: Ehlers–Danlos syndrome results from defective collagen, producing joint hypermobility and fragile, hyperextensible skin. Fibrillin/elastin defects underlie Marfan syndrome instead.

histology__BASIC TISSUES__Connective Tis.question: A patient with Marfan syndrome develops aortic dilatation. The underlying defect is in:
options: Fibrillin (FBN1), a component of elastic fibres
histology__BASIC TISSUES__Connective Tis.explanation: Marfan syndrome is caused by an FBN1 (fibrillin) mutation weakening elastic tissue, predisposing to aortic aneurysm/dissection and lens dislocation.

histology__BASIC TISSUES__Connective Tis.question: Poor wound healing and bleeding gums due to failed collagen cross-linking indicate a deficiency of:
histology__BASIC TISSUES__Connective Tis.explanation: Vitamin C is a cofactor for prolyl/lysyl hydroxylase in collagen synthesis; deficiency (scurvy) impairs collagen cross-linking, causing poor healing and bleeding gums.

histology__BASIC TISSUES__Connective Tis.question: Which cell, when it degranulates in type I hypersensitivity, releases histamine to cause allergy and anaphylaxis?
histology__BASIC TISSUES__Connective Tis.explanation: Mast cells store histamine and heparin; their degranulation in type I hypersensitivity drives allergic reactions and anaphylaxis. They show toluidine-blue metachromasia.

histology__BASIC TISSUES__Connective Tis.question: On a routine H&E section, adipocytes appear as empty 'signet-ring' spaces because:
options: The lipid is dissolved out by the solvents used in processing
histology__BASIC TISSUES__Connective Tis.explanation: Routine processing uses alcohols and xylene, which dissolve the fat, leaving an empty vacuole with the nucleus pushed to the rim. Oil Red O on frozen tissue preserves and stains the lipid.

histology__BASIC TISSUES__Connective Tis.question: Which stain would you request to grade collagen deposition (fibrosis) in a tissue?
histology__BASIC TISSUES__Connective Tis.explanation: Masson's trichrome stains collagen blue/green and is used to assess/grade fibrosis. Congo red is for amyloid, Perls' for iron, ZN for acid-fast bacilli.

histology__BASIC TISSUES__Epithelium (ty.question: How is an epithelium classified/named?
options: By number of cell layers plus the shape of the surface cell
histology__BASIC TISSUES__Epithelium (ty.explanation: Epithelium is named by number of layers (simple/stratified/pseudostratified) and the shape of the surface cell (squamous/cuboidal/columnar). For stratified epithelium, the surface layer determines the name.

histology__BASIC TISSUES__Epithelium (ty.question: A tissue appears layered, but every cell contacts the basement membrane and it bears cilia and goblet cells. What is it, and where is it found?
histology__BASIC TISSUES__Epithelium (ty.explanation: All cells touching the basement membrane with nuclei at different heights = pseudostratified epithelium; ciliated with goblet cells, it lines the respiratory tract (nose, trachea, bronchi).

histology__BASIC TISSUES__Epithelium (ty.question: Which epithelium lines the alveoli, glomerular capsule and blood vessels, suited to diffusion and filtration?
histology__BASIC TISSUES__Epithelium (ty.explanation: Simple squamous epithelium — a single flat layer minimising diffusion distance — lines alveoli (gas exchange), Bowman's capsule (filtration) and vessels (endothelium).

histology__BASIC TISSUES__Epithelium (ty.question: The epithelium of the bladder, which flattens as the organ fills, is:
histology__BASIC TISSUES__Epithelium (ty.explanation: Transitional epithelium (urothelium) lines the bladder and ureters; its dome-shaped umbrella cells flatten on distension, forming a stretchable, impermeable barrier.

histology__BASIC TISSUES__Epithelium (ty.question: Which epithelium provides the dry, protective surface of the skin?
histology__BASIC TISSUES__Epithelium (ty.explanation: Keratinised stratified squamous epithelium (epidermis) has a surface layer of dead, keratin-filled cells providing protection and waterproofing. Non-keratinised lines moist surfaces (mouth, oesophagus, vagina).

histology__BASIC TISSUES__Epithelium (ty.question: Which junction seals the space between epithelial cells to prevent paracellular leakage and maintain polarity?
histology__BASIC TISSUES__Epithelium (ty.explanation: The tight junction (zonula occludens; claudins/occludins) seals the intercellular space, blocking paracellular movement and keeping apical and basolateral domains separate.

histology__BASIC TISSUES__Epithelium (ty.question: Autoantibodies against desmogleins cause loss of which junction, producing intra-epidermal blisters in pemphigus vulgaris?
histology__BASIC TISSUES__Epithelium (ty.explanation: Desmosomes (cadherin–keratin spot-welds) hold keratinocytes together; anti-desmoglein autoantibodies in pemphigus vulgaris break these, causing intra-epidermal blistering.

histology__BASIC TISSUES__Epithelium (ty.question: Which structure anchors the basal epithelial cell to the basement membrane?
histology__BASIC TISSUES__Epithelium (ty.explanation: Hemidesmosomes use integrins to anchor the basal cell surface to the basement membrane; defects cause blistering diseases such as epidermolysis bullosa.

histology__BASIC TISSUES__Epithelium (ty.question: A brush border of microvilli on an absorptive cell serves to:
options: Increase apical surface area for absorption

histology__BASIC TISSUES__Epithelium (ty.explanation: The basal lamina is composed of type IV collagen and laminin (glycoproteins), which are PAS-positive (magenta). It attaches epithelium to connective tissue and acts as a filter.

histology__BASIC TISSUES__Epithelium (ty.explanation: Holocrine secretion (sebaceous glands) involves the whole cell breaking down to release its product. Merocrine uses exocytosis; apocrine pinches off apical cytoplasm.

histology__BASIC TISSUES__Epithelium (ty.explanation: A goblet cell is a single mucus-secreting cell — a unicellular exocrine gland — found in respiratory and intestinal epithelium.

histology__BASIC TISSUES__Epithelium (ty.question: In Barrett's oesophagus, stratified squamous epithelium is replaced by columnar epithelium. This process is called:
histology__BASIC TISSUES__Epithelium (ty.explanation: Metaplasia is the reversible replacement of one differentiated epithelium by another; in Barrett's, chronic acid reflux drives squamous → columnar (intestinal-type) change, a risk factor for adenocarcinoma.
